facts.statement: Paluxysuchus is an extinct neosuchian crocodyliform found in the Early Cretaceous Twin Mountains Formation of north-central Texas.
facts.quote: Paluxysuchus is an extinct genus of neosuchian crocodyliform known from the Early Cretaceous Twin Mountains Formation (late Aptian stage) of north-central Texas.

facts.statement: The genus Paluxysuchus contains only one species, Paluxysuchus newmani.
facts.quote: It contains a single species, Paluxysuchus newmani.

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus is one of three known Early Cretaceous crocodyliforms from Texas, alongside Pachycheilosuchus and an unnamed "Glen Rose Form".
facts.quote: Paluxysuchus is one of three crocodyliforms known from the Early Cretaceous of Texas, the others being Pachycheilosuchus and an unnamed species referred to as the "Glen Rose Form".

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus had a long, flat skull that likely represents a transitional form between early and later neosuchian skull shapes.
facts.quote: Paluxysuchus has a long, flat skull that is probably transitional between the long and narrow skulls of many early neosuchians and the short and flat skulls of later neosuchians.

facts.statement: The skull of Paluxysuchus was long, flat, and triangular in shape when viewed from above.
facts.quote: The skull of Paluxysuchus is long, flat, and shaped somewhat like a triangle when viewed from above.

facts.statement: The most complete skull fossil of Paluxysuchus measures about 30 cm in length.
facts.quote: In the most complete fossil of Paluxysuchus, the skull is about 30 cm long.

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus had enlarged teeth at the tip of its snout.
facts.quote: The teeth at the tip of the snout are enlarged.

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus possessed a postorbital process with an elongated prong bordering the side of the eye socket.
facts.quote: A ridge of bone behind the eye socket called the postorbital process has an elongated prong that borders the side of the socket.

facts.statement: The species Paluxysuchus newmani was named after Kent Newman, who helped excavate and prepare fossils from the Hood County ranch.
facts.quote: The type species of Paluxysuchus, P. newmani, was named after Kent Newman, who was involved in the excavation and preparation of many fossils from the Hood County ranch.

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus belongs to the clade Neosuchia, which includes modern crocodilians and their extinct relatives dating back to the Early Jurassic.
facts.quote: Paluxysuchus belongs to a clade called Neosuchia, which includes living crocodilians and their extinct relatives extending back to the Early Jurassic.

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus is a basal member of Neosuchia, representing one of the earliest branches in the group, though not the oldest.
facts.quote: Paluxysuchus is a basal member of Neosuchia, indicating that it was one of the earliest neosuchians to branch off from the group, although it is not the oldest neosuchian.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Paluxysuchus just outside the group of "derived" neosuchians, which includes modern crocodilians and forms with shortened snouts.
facts.quote: It was found to lie just outside "derived" neosuchians, which include all modern crocodilians and more basal forms characterized by shortened or brevirostrine snouts.

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus had a longirostrine (lengthened) snout, considered a primitive trait among neosuchians.
facts.quote: Paluxysuchus has a lengthened or longirostrine snout, which is considered a primitive condition among neosuchians.

facts.statement: Unlike most primitive longirostrine neosuchians which had tubular snouts, Paluxysuchus had a flattened snout.
facts.quote: However, while most other primitively longirostrine neosuchians have tubular snouts, Paluxysuchus has a flattened or platyrostral snout.

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus was the second crocodyliform named from the Early Cretaceous of Texas, following Pachycheilosuchus.
facts.quote: Paluxysuchus is the second crocodyliform to be named from the Early Cretaceous of Texas, the first being Pachycheilosuchus from the Glen Rose Formation.

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages, approximately 119.57 to 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Albian (119.57 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Paluxysuchus belongs to the family Paluxysuchidae.
